title: Organized Planning: The Crystallization of Desire into Action
coreMove: A failed plan is not failed desire; keep the aim fixed while allies, compensation, harmony, leadership discipline, and fresh plans turn desire into work.

exampleSpecs.audience: Roland, a cafe owner turning desire into a workable expansion plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: A lease option will expire unless the plan gains real allies and structure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the Master Mind alliance becoming roles, compensation, meetings, and harmony.

exampleSpecs.audience: Donna, a dispatch lead judging service value before the night shift
exampleSpecs.stakes: A fast crew is losing repeat business through poor cooperative habits.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Quality, Quantity, and Spirit as a behavioral service audit.

exampleSpecs.audience: Nicholas, a project lead auditing his own leadership after a missed deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: A rollout failure will become blame unless the leader finds his part in the plan.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn the 11 leadership traits and 10 failures into a leadership diagnostic.

exampleSpecs.audience: Arlo, a founder rebuilding a plan after the first prototype fails
exampleSpecs.stakes: Investors will hear the update before the founder has stopped defending the old roadmap.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a failed plan being replaced while the definite aim remains.

exampleSpecs.audience: Zainab, a clinic coordinator protecting cooperation during a staffing shortage
exampleSpecs.stakes: A respected doctor wants command pressure to solve a volunteer shortfall.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast force with cooperative leadership using the leadership traits.

exampleSpecs.audience: Hudson, a consultant revising his service plan before asking for renewal
exampleSpecs.stakes: Strong analysis may not overcome late delivery and a sharp cooperative tone.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use QQS to show why service value includes behavior as well as output.
